title.narrative: Activity under preparation Botswana: Green value chain development for job creation programme

description.narrative: The Green Value Chain Development for Job Creation in Botswana Programme will support Botswana¿s sustainable economic growth and job creation, with a focus on (1) support to the eco-tourism value chain, and (2) support to the horticulture value chain (with a focus on high-value fruits and vegetables). These sectors were strategically chosen for their potential to address key challenges in the country, such as over-reliance on diamond mining, high unemployment rates, and food import dependency. The action is aligned with the EU¿s Multi-Annual Indicative Programme (2021-2027) for Botswana¿s Priority Area 2, which focuses on economic diversification and job creation; and Priority Area 1, which promotes green transformation. By addressing these priorities, the programme also contributes directly to the implementation of Botswana¿s long-term development strategies, in particular its Vision 2036 goal of achieving economic diversification and prosperity for all.¿The programme¿s intervention logic is grounded in the overarching aim of driving economic transformation and creating decent jobs. It seeks to achieve this through a combination of targeted support for the eco-tourism and horticulture value chains and broader efforts to improve the enabling environment for business and investment for these two value chains. For eco-tourism, the programme will enhance community-based tourism initiatives, provide technical assistance to micro small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and strengthen conservation practices to ensure sustainable growth. For horticulture, it will focus on increasing the production of high-value fruits and vegetables through modern farming techniques, capacity building for MSMEs, and improving market access at domestic, regional, and international levels. Direct grants will be awarded to relevant organisations to boost both value chains, taking into account possible interactions and synergies between the two value chains. Both value chains will benefit from interventions aimed at promoting sustainable practices that align with securing access to the EU and other significant markets, such as circularity/recycling, renewable energy use, and eco-certifications, to align with Botswana¿s objectives in this area as well as the EU¿s green agenda and the Global Gateway priorities.The expected results of the programme include a more competitive and sustainable eco-tourism sector that generates decent employment while conserving biodiversity, and a revitalized horticulture sector that reduces dependency on imports, enhances food security, and boosts local supply and exports. These outcomes directly contribute to the trade facilitation objectives of the Global Gateway and to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, including mainly to SDG 8 on decent work and economic growth as well as to SDG 1 on the elimination of poverty, and SDG 12 on responsible consumption and production. Furthermore, the action has significant markers for biodiversity conservation and gender equality, reflecting its commitment to inclusive and environmentally sustainable development. Through this integrated approach, the action will not only address immediate economic and social challenges but also lay the groundwork for a more resilient and diversified economy in Botswana.<
